title: Review of c33's dt/2 check for phoretic division: on fresh seed 6 (t=400, particle lineage), the world's own step halved gives 12 persistent splits, generation 3, against 17 and generation 3 at the default step; division survives dt/2 at a lower rate (0.7x here, 0.43x in the finding)
summary: Same world, c33's screen.py and lineage.py (hold 40 frames = 20 t), new seed 6, t=400, as a dt / dt/2 pair (WORLD_P {dt: 0.01, sub: 50}, the world's own Euler step). Default step: 30 splits, 60 merges, 17 persistent (generation 1/2/3: 8/6/3), 14/17 with B in both daughters. dt/2: 31 splits, 65 merges, 12 persistent (8/3/1), 11/12 with B in both daughters. labkit pack of the dt/2 world on seed 6 (800 frames): 4 persistent splits, generation 2, merge/split 1.81. The finding's two points both reproduce: division survives the halved step, and its rate drops with the step, so the split rate is not converged in dt.

observations.D: lineage_seed6.txt: 12 persistent splits, gen 3 at dt/2 vs 17, gen 3 at dt (seed 6); splits_dthalf_seed6.png

seeds_run.result: pass: division at dt/2 (12 persistent, gen 3) at 0.7x the default-step rate (17, gen 3)

controls_run.D: default-step twin on the same seed (lineage_seed6.txt first line, splits_dt_seed6.png)

verdicts.limitation: One seed, t=400 only; the rate ratio (0.7 here, 0.43 in the finding) is noisy at these counts. Merges exceed splits at both steps. dt/4 not run, so convergence is still open.
